newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian fin min sees 20 pct T-bill yield in 6 mos.
newsitem.headline: Russian fin min sees 20 pct T-bill yield in 6 mos.

text.p: Russian finance minister Alexander Livshits, in newspaper interview published on Thursday, said yields on treasury bills could fall to 20 percent within six months but that Russia would protect its banks.
Moscow's Sevodnya newspaper quoted Livshits in an interview on the transition of the economy from hyperinflation.
Livshits said yields on T-bills, or GKOs, which were over 200 percent earlier in the year and fell below 50 percent on Wednesday, would fall again by more than half.
"Aside from political considerations of lack of will, I do not see anything that would stop Treasury bill yields falling to 20 percent annually within half a year," Livshits said.
But the liberal finance minister said Russia would treat commercial banks, hundreds of which have collapsed over the last year as inflation fell, with kid gloves.
Many Russian banks flourished during high inflation on currency speculation, profiting from investments in the high yielding GKOs, must now adapt to a low inflation environment.
"The government and central bank will support the banking system and help it get through these hard times," Livshits said, referring to the need to adapt to low inflation.
He said the banks were the economy's "weak link" and called them "our children".
